Definition: from G1893 and G1211; since now, i.e. (of time) when, or (of cause) whereas:--after that, because, for (that, -asmuch as), seeing, since.
BiblicalUsage: Epeide means since now, whereas, because — a word for giving the reason things stand as they do. Luke uses it to open a new scene, Paul uses it to explain why God chose foolish preaching to save believers, and why the word went to the Gentiles when it was spoken against.
TheologicalSignificance: Reasons matter to God, and when Scripture says because, I should stop and listen to the reason it gives. I hold that He does not act without cause, and the reasons He gives — foolish preaching, a door opened to the Gentiles — are worth more than my own explanations.
